plans.goal: Light the gorse before the gate to create a wall of fire that frightens the pack back
steps: Secure a fire source—the torch at the camp or steal from the main campfire
Push forward through the fold toward the gorse thicket north of the gate
Light the gorse to create a barrier of flame
The pack flinches and recoils from the burning wall
Close and secure the fold gates against their retreat

atoms.text: Grab the torch, we need fire for the gorse patch
Moving through the fold toward the gorse thicket
Fire the gorse before the gate—now
That wall of flame will send them running
Borin, hold the fold wall, keep them from breaking back in
Push them back hard into the open—they won't stand

plans.goal: Heave the loose fold wall over to crush and block the wolves' escape route
steps: Reach the loose stretch of wall on the northwest section
Heave the wall over outward across 3 rows
Wolves are crushed or blocked by the falling stone
Use the rubble and gap as a tactical advantage
Drive any survivors back out into the brush with nowhere to hide

atoms.text: Moving to the loose wall section, northwest side of the fold
The wall crush zone blocks their escape route north
Push them against the fallen wall, don't let them regroup
We've got them trapped—between the wall and our blades
Drive them out into the brush—they won't come back to this fold

plans.goal: Combine both set-pieces—fire and wall collapse—to trap the pack and force them into complete retreat
steps: Coordinate Pip to light the gorse while you ready the wall
Heave the wall and ring the bell simultaneously for triple chaos
Wolves trapped between flame on north and rubble on south
No escape route, enemies panicked and disoriented
All companions drive them decisively away from the fold

atoms.text: Everyone positions: I'll hit the wall, Pip lights the gorse
Heave the fold wall over now
Fire the gorse, trap them between flame and rubble
The corner is sealed: fire on the north, wall rubble south—nowhere to run
Borin, keep them from breaking through the gap—push hard
All of us together now—drive them out through the brush, they won't return
